parallel.requirements: Recognized ESM-only Node.js output in /output, .mjs suffixes, manual argparse-compatible parsing for --a/--b/--c, no external dependencies, and black-box matching of schedule.every().monday.at(args.a).
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Although launched in swarm mode, the parent performed all work itself after deciding the task was too tightly coupled for useful subagent decomposition; no subagent received ownership.
parallel.implementation: The parent probed valid and invalid executable cases, wrote pyerrors.mjs, schedule.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test4.mjs, then edited argparse.mjs for usage formatting and double-dash behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent wrote all modules into /output with local ESM imports including suffixes; artifact validation later copied test4.mjs and three library modules successfully.
parallel.verification: The parent compared many executable and Node cases, normalized only program name and PyInstaller PID differences, got 29 PASS lines, and ran a final node smoke command.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished implementation is visible at closure; official evaluation completed and passed 70 of 70 samples.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, .mjs, manual argv, no external dependency, black-box schedule behavior, and output parity requirements from the shared prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial main actor owned the entire workflow, first probing the executable and then writing and verifying the implementation directly.
serial.implementation: The actor wrote argparse.mjs, schedule.mjs, and test4.mjs after probing schedule repr, time validation, required arguments, repeated args, unknown args, and help output.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run placed the entry file and two library modules in /output with local ESM imports; artifact validation copied test4.mjs, lib/schedule.mjs, and lib/argparse.mjs successfully.
serial.verification: The serial run compared 12 observed argument scenarios and a help diff against the executable, with all listed checks reporting OK or HELP OK.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished implementation is visible at closure; official evaluation completed and passed 70 of 70 samples.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent received and worked from the full prompt requirements for ESM, .mjs files, manual argv parsing, output parity, and black-box probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent received the same prompt and worked from the same required behaviors and constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirements gap appears; both recognized and satisfied the task contract.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-mode environment enabled swarm mode, but protocol status reports zero direct agent calls, zero subagents, and no delegation; the main actor explicitly kept implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run also had one main actor with swarm mode disabled and no delegation or child ownership.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The only decomposition difference is that the parallel run had swarm mode available but declined to use it; neither run split ownership.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The single parent owned all module contracts and local imports, then adjusted argparse.mjs when verification exposed interface details around usage and double-dash handling.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent likewise kept the module contracts local while writing argparse.mjs, schedule.mjs, and test4.mjs together.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no cross-agent context transfer or interface contract boundary; differences were local implementation choices and iterative fixes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent probed more edge cases, wrote four files including a separate pyerrors helper, then patched argparse formatting and double-dash parsing after comparison failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent probed fewer but sufficient cases and wrote three files with ScheduleValueError and traceback support inside schedule.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced passing implementations; the parallel path was broader and more iterative, while the serial path packaged error support inside schedule.mjs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: There were no child results to retrieve or join; the parent completed its own final response after local verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were likewise no child results; the serial parent completed the prompt directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No result lifecycle coordination difference exists because both modes had a single actor and completed normally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All writes came from the main actor into /output, and artifact validation lists test4.mjs plus three library files as copied successfully.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: All writes came from the main actor into /output, and artifact validation lists test4.mjs plus two library files as copied successfully.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel deliverable had one additional helper module, but there were no concurrent writes, shared-state collisions, or provenance conflicts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent ran a 29-case comparison harness and a final node smoke check before official evaluation passed all 70 samples.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent ran observed-case comparisons plus a help-output diff before official evaluation passed all 70 samples.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was broader, but both had executable-aligned checks and official acceptance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-mode run completed without timeout in 528.869 agent seconds and 584.711 cell seconds, using more requests and tokens than serial.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run completed without timeout in 279.902 agent seconds and 390.298 cell seconds.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel mode cost more time and tokens but did not exhaust budget or leave work unfinished.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluation records passed all 70 samples, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The observable task-solving difference is that the parallel-mode run had swarm mode enabled but performed the whole migration in the main actor after declining delegation, while the serial run also performed the whole migration directly. Both probed the executable, wrote modular ESM output, verified against observed behavior, and delivered accepted artifacts.
parallel_contributors: Direct parent implementation after black-box probing of schedule and argparse behavior.
Broader local comparison harness covering 29 observed cases before closure.
serial_contributors: Direct single-actor implementation after black-box probing of valid, invalid, and help behaviors.
Observed-case comparison and help diff before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used an extra pyerrors.mjs helper and later fixed argparse usage and double-dash handling.
Serial placed ScheduleValueError and traceback support in schedule.mjs and passed with a smaller observed-case suite.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; no retained parallel coordination pattern because no child-agent execution occurred
